title: Dearest of All the Names Above
description: Dearest of All the Names Above in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 148, headed “God reconciled in Christ”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Dear-est of all the names a-bove My Je-sus, and my God, Who can re-sist thy heav-enly love, Or tri-fle with thy blood?

lines: Dearest of all the names above
Who can resist thy heavenly love,
'Tis by the merits of thy death
Till God in human flesh I see,
The holy, just, and sacred Three
His Name forbids my slavish fear,
While Jews on their own law rely,
And there I fix my trust.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
